title: Worker Pools and Backpressure
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose and behavior of worker pools and backpressure.

content.intro: Worker Pools and Backpressure concerns safe coordination among goroutines. Identify the shared state, decide which goroutine owns each value, and choose channels or synchronization primitives intentionally. Bound concurrent work, propagate cancellation with context where appropriate, and test exercised paths with the race detector.
content.why_it_matters: Concurrent code can fail only under particular schedules; explicit ownership, bounded work, cancellation, and race-aware tests improve reliability.

content_blocks.title: Bounded concurrent pipeline
content_blocks.alt_text: A bounded queue and worker count constrain parallel work; context cancellation and error propagation provide a clean stop path. Labeled phases: Producer; Bounded channel; Worker pool; Result + cancellation.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming the happy-path output proves all inputs are safe.
common_mistakes.why: Empty, malformed, boundary, or concurrent cases may follow different paths.
common_mistakes.fix: Add focused tests for a normal input and at least one relevant edge case.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring returned errors or external-system status.
common_mistakes.why: Go APIs commonly report expected failures as explicit error values.
common_mistakes.fix: Check errors close to the operation, add useful context when propagating, and clean up resources.
